title: Kernel pressure simulation and chaos lab manual
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines a repeatable lab and runbook for simulating kernel pressure, injecting controlled chaos into the serving runtime, and capturing profiling + benchmarking artifacts for postmortem and regression detection. The goal is to exercise scheduler heuristics, eviction, KV cache behavior, and fallback routing while preserving reproducibility and safe blast radius.

Scope
-----
- Components exercised: runtime-scheduler, kernel-dispatcher, kvcache-service, observability-sidecar, profiler-agent, perf-bench-suite.
- Environments: staging (default) and isolated canary pool. DO NOT run on production without SRE approval.
- Test types: controlled-pressure (reproducible), stochastic-chaos (fuzz), and benchmark-fidelity (measurement).

Goals and success criteria
-------------------------
- Trigger scheduling preemption and observe kernel handoffs at least once per scenario.
- Produce a profiling bundle with traces, kernel latency histograms, and GPU occupancy snapshots.
- Benchmark results must include p50/p95/p99 latency and per-token cost delta.
- No customer-facing error budget violation in staging: SLOs for the lab are p99 < 300ms for short-run tests and error rate < 0.5%.

Safety and blast-radius controls
------------------------------
1. Always run against the dedicated 'chaos-lab' namespace: label: runtime.lab=chaos.
2. Limit concurrency: max_concurrency=20 for all injected requests.
3. Rate-limit to 10 QPS per kernel variant.
4. Automatic rollback: the chaos harness will set an abort flag on > 1% 5xx across the namespace.

Experiment matrix (canonical scenarios)
--------------------------------------
| Scenario name | Target component | Input signature | Expected observable | When to run |
|---------------|------------------|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| kvcache-thrash | kvcache-service + scheduler | many short prefix-heavy sessions (len 64) | KV eviction spikes, warmup latency increase | weekly regression run |
| small-kernel-starve | kernel-dispatcher | mix of tiny (gen length 8) and medium (gen length 256) | preemptions + batch slicing events | before kernel rollout |
| gpu-fragmentation | runtime-scheduler + GPU pool | interleaved large-seq requests | reduced occupancy, higher tail-latency | quarterly capacity test |
| admission-storm | admission-controller | burst of low-priority payloads | graceful degradation, fair-share enforcement | release candidate gate |

Instrumentation checklist
-------------------------
- profiler-agent: enable delta-sampling at 10kHz for GPU kernels.
- observability-sidecar: capture per-request token counts, kernel-tag, and kvcache-hit.
- runtime-scheduler traces: enable tracer.level=VERBOSE for 2 minutes at scenario start.
- Save kernel metrics to /artifacts/<run-id>/kernel-metrics.json.

Runbook: controlled kernel-pressure test (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------------------------
1. Prepare environment
   a. kubectl ctx staging-1 && kubectl apply -f namespaces/chaos-lab.yaml
   b. Confirm node labels: kubectl get nodes -l runtime.lab=chaos -o wide
2. Deploy harness
   a. helm upgrade --install chaos-harness ./charts/chaos-harness --namespace chaos-lab --set concurrency=10
   b. Start profiler-agent sidecar: kubectl patch deploy runtime-scheduler --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"profiler/enable":"true"}}}}}' -n chaos-lab
3. Start baseline benchmark
   a. perf-bench-suite run --suite baseline --out /artifacts/<run-id>/baseline.json --concurrency 10 --duration 300s
4. Inject pressure
   a. perf-hammer --scenario small-kernel-starve --concurrency 20 --duration 180s --target http://runtime-scheduler.chaos-lab.svc.cluster.local/generate
5. Monitor signals
   a. watch -n 5 'kubectl top pods -n chaos-lab | head -n 20'
   b. tail -f /var/log/observability-sidecar/trace.log | grep kernel-handoff
6. Capture artifacts
   a. kubectl cp chaos-harness:/tmp/profiler-bundle /artifacts/<run-id>/profiler-bundle
   b. perf-bench-suite collect --out /artifacts/<run-id>/post-inject.json
7. Teardown
   a. helm uninstall chaos-harness -n chaos-lab
   b. kubectl patch deploy runtime-scheduler --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"profiler/enable":"false"}}}}}' -n chaos-lab

Diagnostic checks and acceptance criteria
---------------------------------------
- Kernel handoff count >= 1 and visible in tracer.trace_id set.
- KV cache hit-rate delta documented; ideal: <10% sustained drop; otherwise file ticket.
- GPU occupancy snapshots show expected fragmentation pattern for the scenario.
- No more than 0.5% 5xx observed across test window.

Benchmarking suite integration
-----------------------------
- Add a 'chaos-aware' step to perf-bench-suite that runs the experiment in a shadow namespace and applies a scoring function: score = 0.6 * (p99_normalized) + 0.4*(per_token_cost_normalized).
- Store results in bench-db with tags: run_id, scenario, kernel-variant, scheduler-config. Example JSON record: 
{"run_id": "2026-02-04-kps-001",
  "scenario": "small-kernel-starve",
  "kernel_variant": "kv-small-v2-q4",
  "p50_ms": "42",
  "p99_ms": "312"
}

Kernel scheduling config snippets
--------------------------------
Example admission-profile (YAML):
apiVersion: runtime.redwood/v1
kind: KernelAdmissionProfile
metadata:
  name: chaos-lab-profile
spec:
  priorityClasses:
    - name: realtime
      minShare: 0.7
    - name: best-effort
      minShare: 0.1
  preemption:
    enabled: true
    gracePeriodMs: 75
  batchSlicing:
    enabled: true
    maxSlices: 4

Known issues and mitigations (observed during lab)
--------------------------------------------------
- Issue: intermittent tracer storm causing increased control-plane CPU. Mitigation: limit tracer.level windows to 2 minutes and sample 1/100 requests.
- Issue: perf-hammer can saturate NVLink on old nodes. Mitigation: add nodeSelector runtime.gpu.family!=ampere-old for chaos pool.
- Issue: profiler-agent bundle size > 2GB causing cp failures. Mitigation: use streaming upload to artifact-store and compress with zstd.

Release notes (for kernel-pressure harness v1.2.0)
------------------------------------------------
- Added admission-storm and kvcache-thrash scenarios.
- Reduced default harness concurrency to 10 and added automatic abort on >1% 5xx.
- Improved profiler-agent to include GPU callstacks and kernel launch timelines.

Postmortem template (use when a regression is triggered)
-----------------------------------------------------
1. Run metadata: run_id, start_ts, duration, operator.
2. Failure signals: p99 delta, 5xx rate, kernel-handoff-count.
3. Artifacts: profiler-bundle, post-inject.json, scheduler trace.
4. Hypothesis and experiments to validate.
5. Mitigation and rollback steps.

Ownership and escalation
-----------------------
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime / Sofia Patel (oncall alias: runtime-kernel-oncall@redwood.ai).
- Secondary: eng-sre / Ethan Liu.
- For perf-bench anomalies, notify perf-ops channel (#perf-bench).

Appendix: quick commands and snippets
------------------------------------
- Start a scoped tracer window:
  curl -XPOST http://runtime-scheduler.chaos-lab.svc.cluster.local/admin/tracer -d '{"duration_ms":120000, "level":"VERBOSE"}'
- Launch perf-hammer scenario:
  perf-hammer --scenario small-kernel-starve --concurrency 20 --duration 180s --target http://runtime-scheduler.chaos-lab.svc.cluster.local/generate
- Collect artifacts:
  mkdir -p /artifacts/<run-id> && kubectl cp chaos-harness:/tmp/profiler-bundle /artifacts/<run-id>/profiler-bundle && perf-bench-suite collect --out /artifacts/<run-id>/post-inject.json
